question: Does the newly presented NFRDI Lake Naujan assessment publish a reusable, waterbody-resolved fish list for the MIMAROPA rollout?

source.title: NFRDI assessment provides scientific baseline for sustainable management of Lake Naujan fisheries
source.provider: Department of Agriculture - National Fisheries Research and Development Institute
source.access: The official NFRDI search-index result exposed the full text of the summary. Direct page retrieval returned HTTP 502/timeouts in this review, so no downloadable report or linked data table was inspected.

scopeAndCrosswalk.butasRiver: The official summary reports a concern about nets obstructing migratory-fish movement through the Butas River, but does not provide a river survey or station-level fish records.
scopeAndCrosswalk.notMergedWith2025Inventory: The NFRDI 2025 feature describes a separate April-May 2025 inventory across 17 lakeside barangays: 1,302 fishers, 1,079 vessels, and 12 gear types. Those counts are retained as a different activity from the July 2025-June 2026 stock assessment and are not reconciled or combined here.

limits: The summary names 43 documented aquatic taxa but does not expose their list or clarify the mix of finfish and other aquatic groups.
No detailed methods, sampling/landing locations, taxon-by-site crosswalk, voucher evidence, capture dates, full catch table, or underlying dataset was reviewed.
The aggregate 484.87 MT figure does not establish species-specific catch or current distribution at any lake shore, tributary, or Butas River reach.
The publication summary does not state item-specific reuse terms for species-level extraction or public-app display.
The assessment and its fishery-catch context cannot be generalized to all MIMAROPA waters or other Philippine regions.
nextAction: Seek the official taxon list, methods, locality/date structure, supporting taxonomic evidence, and item-specific reuse terms; keep the assessment as an aggregate access lead until those are reviewed.
